note: Card acceptance and payments, Mexico City (the company's 2024 release). 'The previous investors in Clip include General Atlantic LLC, Goldman Sachs Group Inc., Ribbit Capital, Alta Ventures ...' (Nearshore Americas, 2021-06-15, on the $250M Series D), and Ribbit's earliest deal vehicle in Clip is CL-C Ribbit Opportunity IV (Form D, 2020 Q1, coded to the Series C), followed by CL-D in the Series D. No earlier Ribbit round was found and the firm first listed Clip in 2022: the entry reads Growth.

Digital Currency Group, Grayscale's parent (Stamford, Connecticut). Ribbit bought in through the $700 million 2021 secondary: 'SoftBank led the round, with participation from Alphabet's CapitalG and Ribbit Capital', valuing DCG at $10B (CNBC, 2021-11-01), via its DG-S Bullfrog Opportunity II vehicle ($140.8M sold, Form D 2021 Q3): a secondary entry, Growth. The $10B stands as the last priced event, stale, aligned with the Bain Capital Ventures row. Genesis, DCG's lending unit, filed for bankruptcy in January 2023; DCG itself did not, so the row reads private.

Used-car marketplace and auto financing (Mexico City, Wikipedia). Ribbit co-led the $485M Series D of April 2021 at a $4B valuation: 'The round was led by D1 Capital Partners, Founders Fund, Ribbit and BOND' (LatamList), and joined the $700M Series E of September 2021 led by General Catalyst (Bloomberg Linea; its KV-E Bullfrog Opportunity I vehicle, Form D 2021 Q3). No earlier round names Ribbit. The $8.7B Series E mark is superseded by documented collapse evidence: Kavak raised $127M in March 2025 at a $2.2B valuation, led by SoftBank and General Atlantic (Contxto).

note: Thermal battery maker, San Jose (Pulse 2.0; Crunchbase News). The company did not disclose the valuation (Crunchbase News, 2026-07-30), and without a citable priced figure no band from $1B up may be asserted (Rule A): the web check of 2026-09-28 found none, so the row reads below_1b with the check recorded, the round size pointing higher.
